scams.name: The Trevi Fountain Tre Campanelle Sting
scams.description: A 'finto croupier' works three metal shells on a fold-up table near Trevi, the Pantheon or Piazza di Spagna; well-dressed accomplices fake easy €50 wins while pickpocket partners work the onlookers. An April 11, 2025 ANSA report documents Carabinieri arresting a 50-year-old Romanian man and 34-year-old Romanian woman on the Trinità dei Monti steps after a tourist lost €100. A November 29, 2025 Repubblica Roma report details a six-person gang caught near Fontana di Trevi with €1,450 in euros, US dollars and British pounds. A March 29, 2026 ANSA Lazio bulletin denounced 20+ across Pincio, Trevi, Spagna, Pantheon and Piazza di Pietra; Corriere Roma estimates three organised bands in the Tridente earning ~€1,000/hour each.
scams.avoidance: Do not stop, do not watch, do not bet — the game is 'always, always rigged' (r/ItalyTravel, 123 upvotes). Walk past with your hand on your bag zipper — accomplices pickpocket onlookers while the game holds attention. If you see the table forming near a landmark, cross to the opposite side and keep moving. Report the location to 113 (Polizia di Stato) or 112 (Carabinieri) — polizia locale now run masked-officer stings, and your tip helps.
scams.location: Fontana di Trevi, Via delle Muratte, Via in Arcione, Piazza di Pietra, Pantheon, Via del Corso, Piazza di Spagna, Trinità dei Monti, Pincio

scams.name: Termini Station Pickpocket Rings
scams.description: Coordinated Latino, North African and Roma networks work Termini platforms, the underground galleria, Piazza dei Cinquecento and bus 64/40 queues. A March 2025 Repubblica Roma piece names Termini, Colosseo and Barberini as stations 'dove i turisti diventano prede.' An October 2025 Repubblica investigation found a deposito clandestino of stolen suitcases and designer goods in a Termini-area guesthouse. A February 2026 Repubblica report covered the new Polmetro base at Termini (50 agents, 5,000 cameras). Variants include 'helper' scams at ticket machines that photograph card PINs and the 'cavallo di ritorno' phone-ransom extortion (Corriere Roma, November 2022).
scams.avoidance: Buy tickets only on Trenitalia/Italo apps or logo-marked machines — never let a 'helper' touch your card or coins. Use only the signed official taxi rank; refuse 'taxi?' solicitations inside the hall. On Frecciarossa/Italo, put luggage on the end-of-carriage rack that faces your seat. Keep phones out of back or side pockets on platforms. Download the Roma Capitale anti-borseggio app that logged 60 reports in its first six days.
scams.location: Roma Termini platforms, underground galleria, Piazza dei Cinquecento forecourt, Metro A/B interchange, bus 64 and 40 queues

scams.name: The Metro A/B "Finto Malore" Distraction Theft
scams.description: A passenger fakes a sudden malore (fainting/nausea) at the metro doors while a partner lifts wallets from the tourists who lean in to help. Roma Today documents the 7:20am Metro A textbook case; a March 11, 2026 Roma Today arrest report covers three Romanian citizens (two adults plus a 14-year-old minor) caught encircling a tourist on Metro B at Colosseo. Repubblica Roma documented female pickpockets deploying pepper spray on Metro A in March 2025 and Peruvian-on-Peruvian violence at Termini in May 2025. Il Messaggero tracks a 'new generation' of borseggiatori wearing designer clothes and in-ear communications.
scams.avoidance: Ride metro and bus 64 with bag zipped and across the chest on the side opposite the door, one hand on the zipper. Treat any 'malore' at metro doors as a pickpocket distraction first — back up one step. Never carry phone/wallet in back, hip or jacket side pockets on Roman transport. Shout 'ladro!' if groped — Roma Today documents multiple arrests after passenger reactions. Get off at the next station after a suspicious approach; check yourself on the platform.
scams.location: Metro A (Termini–Repubblica–Barberini–Spagna–Flaminio–Ottaviano), Metro B (Termini–Cavour–Colosseo–Circo Massimo), bus 64 Termini–San Pietro

scams.name: The Colosseum Fake Gladiator Photo Shakedown
scams.description: Men in plastic armour and red capes drape props on tourists, pose for 'free' photos, then demand €20–€50+ per person. The racket has been a Rome political scandal for over a decade: Corriere Roma's 2010 Paolo Graldi 'Il caso Centurioni' editorial and Senator Fabrizio Cutrufo's 2011 anti-stalking proposal called for specific legislation. Il Messaggero covers them as a 'banda dei selfie' that also lifts bags in the photo density near the Arco di Costantino. r/rome's moderator-linked thread confirms the operators 'are part of an organised racket' documented by AGTAR (Association for Certified Tour Guides in Rome) and Il Messaggero journalists. Parallel fake-guide pattern: February 2026 Repubblica Roma documents three finti Ciceroni from Iran and Brazil fined €400 each.
scams.avoidance: Book Colosseum, Forum and Palatine tickets in advance at coopculture.it, the Parco Archeologico app, or a verified operator — never buy from someone in costume. Say 'no, grazie' and keep walking; do not pause, do not shake hands, do not let anything be draped on you. If money is demanded after you refused, say 'chiamo la polizia' and dial 113. Wear your backpack on your front along the Fori Imperiali–Colosseo corridor.
scams.location: Piazza del Colosseo, Via dei Fori Imperiali, Arco di Costantino, Piazza Venezia, Altare della Patria steps

scams.name: The Fiumicino Fake Taxi & Fixed-Fare Scam
scams.description: Rome's official fixed fare is €50 from FCO and €30 from Ciampino (CIA) to inside the Aurelian Walls — but drivers routinely overcharge. A July 2022 Corriere Roma report documented €70 in cash for the FCO-centre fare with the farewell 'Benvenuto a Roma.' A July 2025 r/rome thread documented a driver branded 'Società Cooperativa Roma' demanding €55 for a 3.7-km FCO hop with the meter off, claiming card payments required the passenger to cover 'all commission fees.' An April 2024 Corriere Roma report named a driver forcing a 'tariffa fissa' cash-only; an August 2024 Corriere report documented a driver demanding €200 to return a forgotten laptop. The 'card reader broken' variant is documented across r/rome and r/ItalyTravel.
scams.avoidance: From FCO, take the Leonardo Express (€14, 32 min, every 15 minutes) to Termini — nothing to negotiate. If you must taxi, use only the signed official rank outside arrivals; confirm the €50 (FCO) or €30 (Ciampino) fixed fare before closing the door. Use FREE NOW or itTaxi apps — the meter runs on the app. Always demand a ricevuta with taxi number, date, time, route. Never let a driver take you to an ATM; pay cash for the posted fare and file a complaint at the Comune di Roma Ufficio Taxi.
scams.location: Fiumicino Leonardo da Vinci (FCO) arrivals, Ciampino (CIA) taxi rank, Termini rank at Piazza dei Cinquecento, Piazza San Pietro taxi queue

scams.name: The Vatican Museums "Fake Staff" Line-Jumper
scams.description: Men in uniforms, lanyards and name tags sort the Vatican Museums queue on the street and steer tourists to 'partner offices' for overpriced tickets or cash shakedowns. r/ItalyTravel's 124-upvote 'Scammers at Vatican Museums line!' post lays out the MO — the 'staff' look 'legit' with uniforms and name tags, police stand meters away without intervening. A parallel St. Peter's Square variant sells paid skip-the-line access to the basilica (which is actually free). February 2026 Repubblica Roma fined three finti Ciceroni €400 each at the Colosseum — the same fake-authority pattern at a parallel site. The Vatican's official policy: skip-the-line is sold only via tickets.museivaticani.va or authorised resellers.
scams.avoidance: Buy Vatican Museums tickets only from tickets.museivaticani.va, preferably in advance with a reserved entry time. Ignore anyone on Viale Vaticano; walk to the queue at the door. If you must buy day-of, buy inside the museum building. Basilica entry is free — there is no legitimate 'skip-the-line' for it. Report sidewalk 'staff' to the Gendarmeria Vaticana at the entrance or call 112.
scams.location: Viale Vaticano entrance to the Vatican Museums, Piazza San Pietro colonnade queue, Via di Porta Angelica, Borgo Pio

scams.name: The Bracelet & Rose Aggression (Spanish Steps, Ponte Sant'Angelo, St. Peter's)
scams.description: A friendly stranger opens with 'where are you from?', praises your country, and ties a friendship bracelet (or hands a rose) 'as a gift' — then demands €20 and escalates with shoves, curses or stalking when refused. r/rome's 'Elephant bracelet scam?' thread documents the textbook opening; r/rome's 'Vent: Scam artist had the nerve to TOUCH ME' thread documents a Ponte Sant'Angelo arm-poking incident with fisticuffs. Commenters report being shoved, cursed as a 'bitch,' and having partners robbed the same day in Trastevere after a bracelet-guy approach turned physical. Il Messaggero's centro-storico dossier counted 54 borseggiatori arrested in a single Ferragosto-to-autumn window in the same tourist perimeter.
scams.avoidance: Do not make eye contact, do not reply, do not slow your pace — 'no, grazie' once, then keep moving. Keep hands at your sides or in pockets when bracelet/rose sellers approach; a hand out to 'receive' is the cue they use. If something is placed on you, take it off and drop it — you owe nothing. Zip your bag across your chest in Spanish Steps, Piazza San Pietro and Ponte Sant'Angelo zones (all also pickpocket zones). Dial 113/112 if shoved or followed.
scams.location: Spanish Steps (Piazza di Spagna, Trinità dei Monti), Ponte Sant'Angelo, St. Peter's Square, Piazza Navona, Fontana di Trevi perimeter

scams.name: The Trevi / Pantheon / Piazza Navona Tourist-Menu Trap
scams.description: Restaurants in the Trevi-Pantheon-Navona axis hit tourists with unrequested pane/acqua/antipasti, coperto over €3/head, automatic 15–22% 'servizio' on foreign cards, and branzino priced 'al etto' that arrives at 400–600g. An August 2014 Corriere Roma / Cook piece documented US tourists James and Mariann charged €42 for three gelatos and a bottle of water near Fontana di Trevi. A 2025 r/RomeTravel thread documents a $2,000 restaurant bill for two tourists near Trevi. A parallel 2025 r/ItalyTravel 'Guilt Trap Pharmacy' post documents €20 for two €2.50 thermal patches near Piazza di Pasquino.
scams.avoidance: Walk 5–7 minutes off the Trevi/Pantheon/Navona axis — Monti, Pigneto, Testaccio, southern Trastevere and Prati are locally recommended. Photograph the posted outdoor menu before sitting (Italian law requires prices); if fish/steak is only 'al etto' without portion guidance, leave. Ask at seating 'Mi conferma il coperto e se il servizio è incluso?' Refuse unrequested items — you are not legally required to pay for pane/acqua/antipasti you did not order. Sort Google Maps reviews by 'Most recent' and Italian language.
scams.location: Alleys around Fontana di Trevi, Piazza Navona, Pantheon, Campo de' Fiori, Via della Pace, Via del Governo Vecchio, Piazza di Spagna perimeter

scams.name: The Fake Five-Star Hotel & Off-Platform Rental Scam
scams.description: Scammers create falsi profili mimicking Rome's five-star hotels and vacation rentals to harvest card numbers and up-front payments for reservations that don't exist. A December 13, 2022 ANSA/Corriere Roma investigation documented 200+ American victims; the Corinthia Hotel was named in court documents and US intelligence became involved. A March 16, 2025 Corriere Roma report confirmed 20 people rinviati a giudizio for the continuing scheme. An August 2025 ANSA report documented a €2,700 casa vacanze inesistente in the same playbook at lower price points. Booking.com phishing campaigns (Corriere April 2026) add impersonation risk. Off-platform WhatsApp/email contacts and cash 'security fees' on arrival are the recurring tell.
scams.avoidance: Book hotels only at the property's official site or major aggregators (Booking/Expedia/Marriott/IHG/Hilton apps) — never via a cold email or search-ad URL that doesn't match the hotel's domain. Confirm reservations by calling the hotel's own published number (not the one in the email) and reading your code to reception. For apartments, use Airbnb/Booking/Vrbo only — never wire money to a host. Google Street View every address. Rome's tourism tax is €7/night (€10 at 5-stars) per person and collected only by registered accommodations.
scams.location: Bookings naming Corinthia, Hassler, Cavalieri, Eden and other Rome five-stars; Airbnb listings in Prati, Trastevere and the centro storico

scams.name: The POS Pirata Contactless Skimmer
scams.description: A wireless POS hidden in a bag reads contactless cards and phone wallets through fabric within a few centimetres. An August 1, 2025 Repubblica Roma report documented the Rome arrest of a female thief for indebito utilizzo di strumenti di pagamento. A July 25, 2025 Rainews TGR Campania investigation arrested a 36-year-old Peruvian woman in Sorrento with numerosi precedenti penali a Roma — in one Rome incident she had used a similar device to take ~€9,000 from a single tourist. A July 31, 2025 Corriere Tecnologia explainer confirms attacks operate below the €50/€100 tap thresholds that bypass PIN/face-ID. Low severity reflects the still-modest incident count; per-incident losses are unusually large.
scams.avoidance: Carry contactless cards in an RFID-blocking wallet in Rome's crowded zones (under €15). Disable NFC on cards you don't need daily via your bank app; leave only one card contactless-active. Lower the daily tap limit in your bank app to €25–€50. Use phone wallets (Apple Pay / Google Pay) for in-store purchases — device-bound tokenisation makes POS-pirata attacks much harder. Enable real-time transaction alerts and review on the spot — losses become irreversible only if unreported for hours.
scams.location: Metro A/B carriages, Termini underground galleria, Fontana di Trevi perimeter, Piazza Navona, Piazza di Spagna, bus 64/40
